Raises the cap on the state's Budget Stabilization Account from 10% to 20% of General Fund tax revenue and requires saving more in high-revenue years.
Repeals the ban on public financing of campaigns, letting state and local governments create programs such as small-dollar matching or democracy vouchers.
Removes the replacement-candidate question from state recall ballots; a recalled office would be filled through normal succession rules.
Would require government ID for in-person voting, partial ID numbers on mail-ballot envelopes, and re-registration of millions of voters.
One-time 5% tax on residents with net worth over $1 billion, funding Medi-Cal, public education and food assistance.
Prop 41: New State Taxes & Spending Limit; Audits of Special Taxes
Prohibits excluding new special-tax revenue from the state spending limit and requires audits of programs funded by special taxes.
Prop 42: Bans New State Personal Property Taxes & Certain Retroactive Taxes
Constitutional ban on retroactive taxes and future wealth taxes, restricting how future state tax proposals can pass.
Prop 43: Higher Threshold for Local Taxes
Raises the approval threshold for voter-proposed local special taxes from a simple majority to two-thirds.
Requires nonprofit community clinics to spend at least 90% of revenue on direct program services, with penalties for noncompliance.
Sets strict deadlines on environmental reviews, limits public comment periods and caps judicial review for designated projects.
Updates Berkeley's charter election rules: lower filing fees, public-financing allocations, recall, petition and referendum procedures.
Adopts ranked-choice (instant runoff) voting for mayor and city council elections.
Measure EE: City Administration Charter Amendment
Cuts full City Council meetings to once a week, raises the referendum signature threshold from 10% to 15%, and other changes.
Measure LA: Infrastructure Planning Charter Amendment
Modernizes infrastructure management and expands Public Works authority and municipal property use.
Measure PL: City Planning Department Charter Amendment
Gives the Planning Department explicit authority over quasi-judicial applications and streamlines planning timelines.
Measure PRK: Parks Funding Charter Amendment
Gradually doubles dedicated Recreation and Parks funding over ten years, prioritizing park-poor neighborhoods.
Measure PRT: Airport, Harbor & DWP Charter Amendment
Adjusts governance of proprietary departments, including waterfront public access funding and workforce impact disclosures.
Measure A: Binding Arbitration for Labor Disputes
Adds binding arbitration for public-safety employee labor disputes that reach an impasse.
Strengthens the County Ethics Commission and permanently protects Measure J's 10% allocation to community investment and alternatives to incarceration.
Measure SC: Board of Education Campaign Finance
Applies contribution limits, fundraising windows and disclosure rules to LAUSD board elections.
Adds council oversight of certain appointments, allows an independent budget analyst, and expands the Public Ethics Commission.
Restructures or consolidates departments and commissions and moves commissions from the charter into municipal code.
Proposition B: Municipal Finance Corporation & Public Bank
Authorizes a public bank with community representation and restrictions on investing in weapons, prisons, predatory lending and fossil fuels.
Proposition D: Ballot Measure Process Changes
Proposition F: Executive Branch Management Changes
Changes how the executive branch is organized, including the mayor's authority over department leadership and reorganizations.
Measure AA: Affirmation of Rights Charter Amendment
Affirms the County's commitment to dignity, civil rights and equal protection.
Measure U: Supervisorial Redistricting Charter Amendment
Establishes an independent process for drawing supervisorial district boundaries.
Would change the city treasurer from an elected to an appointed position.
